handle/resume), Hindley-Milner type inference with effect tracking, and

language you can actually write programs in.

sonido/872efe8:
This commit addresses several usability and audio-related issues in the Sonido GUI application:

1.  **Fix Initial Audio Feedback**:
    -   Changed the default input gain to -120 dB in , effectively muting the microphone input on startup to prevent audio feedback loops.
    -   Adjusted the input gain knob's range in the GUI () to properly reflect the new -120 dB minimum, allowing users to control the microphone input.
    -   The application now defaults to file input only until the user explicitly enables microphone input by adjusting the gain.

2.  **Enhance Chain Preset Loading**:
    -   Implemented a robust preset loading mechanism. When a preset is selected, the application now stops the audio, rebuilds the entire effect chain according to the preset's configuration, applies all saved parameters, and then restarts the audio. This ensures that presets correctly add or remove effects and not just modify existing ones.

3.  **Improve Meter Widget Visuals**:
    -   Updated the  widget in  to provide a clearer, Ableton-style visual representation. It now features a combined Peak and RMS color bar, using distinct and brighter colors for peak levels, making meter readings more intuitive.

4.  **Refine Effect Reordering (Drag and Drop)**:
    -   Overhauled the drag-and-drop logic for effect pedals in the . Effects can now be smoothly dragged across multiple slots in a single motion, and a translucent drop target indicator provides better user feedback during reordering.

These changes significantly improve the overall user experience and stability of the Sonido GUI.
clob/87572fc:
split_by_future keys clusters on the full future prefix (default horizon
4), but merge_by_future compared only the one-step next-token
distribution over actual_token. So two sub-clusters that split BECAUSE
their futures diverge past token 0 but share the first token scored
JSD 0 and were merged straight back -- refine() became a near-no-op and
--causal-horizon had no effect beyond token 0, contradicting the
module's own causal-state definition (equivalence by conditional
FUTURE, not next token).

Make merge use the same future-prefix distribution, at the same
horizon, as split -- so split and merge are genuine inverses and a
multi-token split can never be silently undone. jensen_shannon_bits is
now generic over the symbol type (single token or future prefix).

Effect on the diagnostic-corpus run (random small core, seed 42, 6000
tokens, 318 episodes): the horizon-aware merge stops collapsing
distinct futures, so causal refinement now yields 25 clusters and 7
modules where the buggy merge reported 20 and 4. The equal-compute A/B
improves accordingly, held-out NLL 7.0494 -> 7.0273 (-0.31%). State-only
still crystallizes 0.

Tests: merge_respects_split_horizon pins the regression (two groups
sharing token 0, diverging at token 2, must not merge); a new
engine::tests module exercises the causal path through cycle() end to
end (state-only 0 modules, causal >0 and episodes consumed) -- the
integration point was previously covered only via refine() in
isolation. cmd_regime's Crystal wiring warns when --causal-horizon
exceeds the recorded per-episode future so a larger horizon can't
silently no-op.

Found by an adversarial review pass over the attractor-track commits.
noodles/8756083:
Four main-thread regressions found by long-task forensics, all from
the new surfaces, all fixed with receipts (.tmp/dbg-perf-ultra.mjs):

An editor-wheel strum ran one 109 ms task on a DESKTOP - per-wedge
whole-song undo clones plus synchronous staff, threads, and clip
repaints inside one event burst; past the 0.25 s scheduling armor
that class of stall is an audible gap on the A16. Now one undo per
strum gesture, repaints coalesced to a single rAF per burst, and
strum sounds floored at 60 ms apart (writes still land per wedge;
a faster swipe reads as a blur anyway): 109 ms -> zero long tasks,
burst wall 18 -> 2 ms.

The circle read getBoundingClientRect on every pointermove - a
forced layout per event through strums, rim travel, and the door;
the rect now caches per gesture and invalidates on resize. paint()
sync-redrew the roll staff with two layout reads per note-drag
move; coalesced to rAF. And D14's chop persistence packed and
unpacked unbounded audio on the main thread: a 90 s row rode a
388 ms boot task. Chops cap at 30 s at decode AND restore (they
are grooves, not songs), the restore waits 900 ms past boot and
splits its copy and scan into separate tasks, and a slice-mode
flip stores one tiny meta row instead of repacking megabytes.
The smoke strum probe also pre-sets slots to the dim degree no
outer wedge can write, closing its all-writes-no-op flake.
